question: Given the recent confirmation of an atypical case of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) in Ireland, and the swift reactions of trade partners, including the suspension of imports of beef by South Korea, this situation raises serious concerns with regard to both market stability and the confidence of consumers and external partners. Against this backdrop: 1.

What immediate measures does the Commission intend to take to prevent the spread of health risks and to maintain confidence in food chain safety at EU level, and what tools is the Commission considering to limit the impact on European beef exports and avoid disproportionate reactions by third countries?
Given that there is currently no effective treatment or widely available vaccine for BSE, what prevention and control measures are being prioritised at European level to reduce future risks?
Is the Commission considering stepping up investments in research and innovation, including the development of a possible vaccine or advanced disease diagnosis and control methods?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.8.2026) Prevention, control and eradication measures for bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) are laid down in Regulation (EC) No 999/20011. Ensuring the effective implementation of these measures remains a priority for the Commission.

To this end, the Commission has monitored the situation in cooperation with the competent authorities of the Member States to ensure that following the confirmation of a BSE case, whether classical or atypical, all measures under that Regulation were implemented to mitigate any health risk.

Detection of an atypical case of BSE does not affect a country's negligible risk status under the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) and does not justify restrictions on international trade. The co-funded European Partnership on Animal Health and Welfare (EUPAHW)2 was launched in 2024 with an overall budget of EUR 354 million for 10 years.

Under priority 2, it supports research and innovation for animal health and welfare. The EraBSE project3, launched in December 2025 for 36 months, aims to develop tools for surveillance, epidemiological investigation and control of future cases of animal prion diseases.
1 Regulation (EC) No 999/2001 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 May 2001 laying down

rules for the prevention, control and eradication of certain transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (OJ L 147, 31.5.2001, pp. 1–40; ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2001/999/oj). 2 https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101136346. 3 https://www.eupahw.eu/projects/procedures-methodologies-and-tools-to-analyse-animal-health-andwelfare/eradication-of-bse-improving-tools-for-detection-and-management-of-genetic-and-environmental-risks.
